### `cloud.computedriven.com/assets/site.css`

```css
/* cloud.computedriven.com — shares computedriven.com's tokens verbatim so the
   two read as one property. Fonts are self-hosted there for a reason the root
   site states; this surface inherits the same files. */

/* Same two variable woff2 files the root site self-hosts, same reason: a page
   arguing for machines you control should not fetch from one you do not.
   `font-weight: 400 700` is what makes a single variable file cover the range —
   declaring one weight silently flattens every bold on the page. */
@font-face {
    font-family: "Space Grotesk";
    font-style: normal;
    font-weight: 400 700;
    font-display: swap;
    src: url("/fonts/space-grotesk.woff2") format("woff2");
}
@font-face {
    font-family: "JetBrains Mono";
    font-style: normal;
    font-weight: 400 700;
    font-display: swap;
    src: url("/fonts/jetbrains-mono.woff2") format("woff2");
}

:root {
    --bg: #03040a;
    --surface: #0a0c14;
    --surface-2: #10131d;
    --border: rgba(242, 193, 78, 0.14);
    --border-soft: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07);
    --text: #e8e6e0;
    --dim: #8d8b9c;
    --muted: #4a4859;
    --amber: #f2c14e;
    --cyan: #2de2e6;
    --bronze: #a8763e;
    --red: #ff5c5c;
    --sans: "Space Grotesk", system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
    --mono: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace;
    --max-w: 1080px;
    --gutter: clamp(1.25rem, 4vw, 3rem);
}

*,
*::before,
*::after {
    box-sizing: border-box;
}

html {
    -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%;
}

body {
    margin: 0;
    background: var(--bg);
    color: var(--text);
    font-family: var(--sans);
    font-size: clamp(1rem, 0.96rem + 0.2vw, 1.0625rem);
    line-height: 1.65;
    -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
}

/* ── the site header ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Sticky, and deliberately so. amp-nav's _offsetHostFixedNavs() pushes the
   host site's own bar below the portfolio bar by setting `top`, and it only
   touches elements whose COMPUTED position is `fixed` or `sticky` — `top` is a
   no-op on static boxes and would shift a relative one out of place. A static
   header here would look right at first paint and then be overlapped the
   instant amp-nav mounts. */
header.site {
    position: sticky;
    top: 0;
    z-index: 50;
    background: rgba(3, 4, 10, 0.82);
    backdrop-filter: blur(10px);
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
}
.site-bar {
    max-width: var(--max-w);
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 0 var(--gutter);
    height: 56px;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: clamp(0.75rem, 2.4vw, 1.5rem);
}
/* The logo points at the root domain, not at `/` — the three product sites funnel
   back to the studio, and "Overview" one link along is already the way back to
   this site's own front page. The suffix is what keeps the visible label honest
   about the destination; the aria-label carries it at every width, because the
   suffix collapses on narrow screens and an accessible name reading "[World]
   Cloud" on a link that leaves the domain is the actual defect. */
.site-logo {
    flex: none;
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-weight: 700;
    font-size: 0.9rem;
    color: var(--text);
    text-decoration: none;
    white-space: nowrap;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 0.5rem;
}
.site-logo b {
    color: var(--amber);
}
.site-logo:hover {
    color: var(--text);
}
.site-logo:hover b {
    color: var(--cyan);
}
.site-logo .bto {
    font-weight: 400;
    font-size: 0.68rem;
    letter-spacing: 0.04em;
    color: var(--muted);
    transition: color 0.18s ease;
}
.site-logo:hover .bto {
    color: var(--amber);
}
@media (max-width: 860px) {
    .site-logo .bto-w {
        display: none;
    }
}

/* The links scroll inside the bar on a narrow screen rather than wrapping it
   to two rows or pushing the auth control off the right edge. */
.site-links {
    flex: 1 1 auto;
    min-width: 0;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: clamp(0.7rem, 2.2vw, 1.5rem);
    overflow-x: auto;
    scrollbar-width: none;
}
.site-links::-webkit-scrollbar {
    display: none;
}
.site-links a {
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 0.68rem;
    letter-spacing: 0.14em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: var(--dim);
    text-decoration: none;
    white-space: nowrap;
}
.site-links a:hover {
    color: var(--text);
}
.site-links a[aria-current="page"] {
    color: var(--amber);
}

.site-auth {
    flex: none;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 0.55em;
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 0.7rem;
    letter-spacing: 0.1em;
    color: var(--text);
    text-decoration: none;
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius: 3px;
    padding: 0.55em 0.9em;
    white-space: nowrap;
}
.site-auth:hover,
.site-auth[aria-current="page"] {
    border-color: var(--amber);
    color: var(--amber);
}
/* The rung tag beside "Sign in" is written by tools/render-status.mjs from
   status.json — never typed. When portal sign-in leaves `spec` the renderer
   stops emitting it and the control becomes a plain CTA on every page at once. */
.site-auth .tag {
    font-size: 0.85em;
    letter-spacing: 0.05em;
    color: var(--muted);
    border-left: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    padding-left: 0.65em;
}
.site-auth:hover .tag {
    color: inherit;
}

main {
    max-width: var(--max-w);
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 0 var(--gutter) 6rem;
}

section {
    padding-block: clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 4.5rem);
    border-top: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
}
section:first-of-type {
    border-top: 0;
}

h1,
h2,
h3 {
    line-height: 1.12;
    letter-spacing: -0.02em;
    text-wrap: balance;
    margin: 0 0 0.6em;
}
h1 {
    font-size: clamp(2.4rem, 1.4rem + 4.4vw, 4.5rem);
    font-weight: 700;
}
h2 {
    font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 1.2rem + 1.3vw, 2.1rem);
}
h3 {
    font-size: 1.15rem;
    color: var(--amber);
}
p {
    margin: 0 0 1.1em;
    max-width: 68ch;
}

a {
    color: var(--cyan);
    text-underline-offset: 0.2em;
    text-decoration-thickness: 1px;
}
a:hover {
    color: var(--amber);
}
:focus-visible {
    outline: 2px solid var(--amber);
    outline-offset: 3px;
}

code,
kbd {
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 0.86em;
    color: var(--dim);
}

.lede {
    font-size: clamp(1.1rem, 1rem + 0.6vw, 1.4rem);
    color: var(--dim);
    max-width: 60ch;
}
.thesis {
    color: var(--amber);
}
.dim {
    color: var(--dim);
}

/* the honest banner. Amber, not red: this is the system telling the truth
   about itself, which is the system working. */
.banner {
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-left: 3px solid var(--amber);
    background: var(--surface);
    padding: 1rem 1.15rem;
    border-radius: 3px;
    font-size: 0.95rem;
    color: var(--dim);
    max-width: 68ch;
}
.banner strong {
    color: var(--text);
}
.banner b {
    color: var(--amber);
    font-weight: 600;
}

/* ASCII figures. Every one scrolls inside itself so the page body never does. */
figure.fig {
    margin: 1.75rem 0;
    border: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    background: var(--surface);
    border-radius: 3px;
    overflow: hidden;
}
figure.fig pre {
    margin: 0;
    padding: 1.25rem;
    overflow-x: auto;
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: clamp(0.66rem, 0.55rem + 0.4vw, 0.8rem);
    line-height: 1.5;
    color: var(--dim);
    tab-size: 4;
}
figure.fig figcaption {
    padding: 0.6rem 1.25rem;
    border-top: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    font-size: 0.82rem;
    color: var(--muted);
}

.grid {
    display: grid;
    gap: 1rem;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 15rem), 1fr));
    padding: 0;
    margin: 1.75rem 0;
    list-style: none;
}
.card {
    border: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    background: var(--surface);
    border-radius: 3px;
    padding: 1.1rem 1.2rem;
}
.card h3 {
    margin-bottom: 0.35em;
    font-size: 1rem;
}
/* A linked card heading stays a heading. Without this it inherits link cyan and
   the grid reads as a row of links rather than a row of cards. */
.card h3 a {
    color: inherit;
    text-decoration-color: var(--muted);
}
.card h3 a:hover {
    color: var(--cyan);
    text-decoration-color: currentColor;
}
.card p {
    margin: 0;
    font-size: 0.92rem;
    color: var(--dim);
}

/* the family band — the same three cards, in the same order and the same words,
   ship on all three product sites and in the root's funnel figure, so a reader
   crossing between them recognises the shape rather than re-learning it. The card
   for the site you are already on is a <div>, not an <a>: a link to the page you
   are on is a link that does nothing, and marking it "you are here" while still
   making it clickable is worse than either. */
.fam {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 14.5rem), 1fr));
    gap: 1rem;
    margin: 1.75rem 0 0;
}
.fam-card {
    display: block;
    text-decoration: none;
    border: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    background: var(--surface);
    border-radius: 3px;
    padding: 1.1rem 1.2rem;
    transition:
        border-color 0.18s ease,
        background 0.18s ease;
}
a.fam-card:hover {
    border-color: var(--cyan);
    background: var(--surface-2);
}
.fam-card .fc-n {
    display: flex;
    align-items: baseline;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 0.5rem;
    font-weight: 700;
    font-size: 1rem;
    color: var(--text);
}
.fam-card .fc-d {
    display: block;
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 0.74rem;
    color: var(--dim);
    margin-top: 0.32rem;
}
.fam-card .fc-h {
    display: block;
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 0.68rem;
    color: var(--muted);
    margin-top: 0.55rem;
}
.fam-card.here {
    border-color: rgba(242, 193, 78, 0.45);
    background: var(--surface-2);
}
.fam-card.here .fc-n {
    color: var(--amber);
}
.fc-you {
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 0.6rem;
    letter-spacing: 0.14em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: var(--amber);
    border: 1px solid rgba(242, 193, 78, 0.4);
    border-radius: 3px;
    padding: 0.08rem 0.4rem;
}
.fam-foot {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    align-items: baseline;
    gap: 0.4rem 0.9rem;
    margin: 1.2rem 0 0;
    padding-top: 1rem;
    border-top: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 0.75rem;
    color: var(--muted);
    max-width: none;
}
.fam-foot a {
    color: var(--amber);
}
.fam-foot a:hover {
    color: var(--cyan);
}

/* tables — wide content scrolls in its own container */
.scroll {
    overflow-x: auto;
    margin: 1.75rem 0;
    border: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    border-radius: 3px;
}
table {
    border-collapse: collapse;
    width: 100%;
    min-width: 40rem;
    font-size: 0.9rem;
}
table caption {
    text-align: left;
    padding: 0.9rem 1rem;
    color: var(--muted);
    font-size: 0.82rem;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
}
th,
td {
    text-align: left;
    padding: 0.6rem 1rem;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    vertical-align: top;
}
thead th {
    color: var(--muted);
    font-size: 0.78rem;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    letter-spacing: 0.06em;
    font-weight: 500;
}
tbody th {
    font-weight: 500;
    color: var(--text);
}
td.num {
    font-family: var(--mono);
    text-align: right;
}
tbody tr:last-child th,
tbody tr:last-child td {
    border-bottom: 0;
}

.rung {
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 0.74rem;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    letter-spacing: 0.05em;
    padding: 0.15em 0.5em;
    border-radius: 2px;
    border: 1px solid currentColor;
    white-space: nowrap;
}
.rung-live {
    color: var(--cyan);
}
.rung-staged {
    color: var(--bronze);
}
.rung-local {
    color: var(--amber);
}
.rung-spec {
    color: var(--muted);
}

.legend {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: auto 1fr;
    gap: 0.5rem 1rem;
    align-items: baseline;
    margin: 1.5rem 0;
    font-size: 0.9rem;
}
.legend dt {
    justify-self: start;
}
.legend dd {
    margin: 0;
    color: var(--dim);
}

nav.pages {
    border-top: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    padding: 1.5rem 0 0;
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 0.5rem 1.5rem;
    font-size: 0.92rem;
}
nav.pages [aria-current="page"] {
    color: var(--amber);
    text-decoration: none;
}

footer {
    max-width: var(--max-w);
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 2rem var(--gutter) 4rem;
    border-top: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    color: var(--muted);
    font-size: 0.85rem;
}
footer p {
    max-width: 68ch;
}

/* The same four-way row is in the footer of all three product sites and the root,
   so the way out is in the same place wherever a reader stops. The property you
   are on is a <b>, not an <a> — see the note on .fam-card. This sits OUTSIDE the
   STATUS: markers on purpose: render-status.mjs rewrites what is between them. */
.foot-fam {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 0.4rem 1.4rem;
    align-items: baseline;
    margin-top: 1.4rem;
    padding-top: 1.2rem;
    border-top: 1px solid var(--border-soft);
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 0.75rem;
}
.foot-fam .ff-links {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 0.3rem 1rem;
}
.foot-fam .ff-links b {
    font-weight: 400;
    color: var(--amber);
}
.foot-fam .ff-links a {
    color: var(--dim);
    text-decoration: none;
}
.foot-fam .ff-links a:hover {
    color: var(--amber);
}

/* The foot of every page ends at the same door. The line under it is generated
   from status.json for the same reason the header tag is: a footer repeated on
   six pages is six places for one fact to go stale. */
.foot-auth {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    align-items: baseline;
    gap: 0.6rem 1.1rem;
    margin: 0 0 1.5rem;
    padding: 1.1rem 1.2rem;
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-left: 3px solid var(--amber);
    border-radius: 3px;
    background: var(--surface);
}
.foot-auth .foot-auth-cta {
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 0.78rem;
    letter-spacing: 0.08em;
    color: var(--text);
    text-decoration: none;
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius: 3px;
    padding: 0.5em 0.9em;
    white-space: nowrap;
}
.foot-auth .foot-auth-cta:hover {
    border-color: var(--amber);
    color: var(--amber);
}
.foot-auth .foot-auth-note {
    flex: 1 1 20ch;
    margin: 0;
    color: var(--dim);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    * {
        animation: none !important;
        transition: none !important;
    }
}
```

### `scripts/cloud-status-counts.mjs`

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Derive the numbers in cloud.computedriven.com/status.json from the tree, and
// refuse to agree with them when they are wrong.
//
// WHY THIS EXISTS. status.json said "10 migrations apply clean" while the tree
// held 12, and a battery check asserted "all six tenant tables" while there were
// nine. Both numbers were true when they were typed. Neither was re-derived.
//
// The repository already has this law from the box-and-box law counts --
//
//     DERIVE THE TOTAL. NEVER HAND-TYPE IT.
//
// -- and this is that law applied to the Cloud status surface, which is the one
// public artifact whose whole purpose is to be accurate about what exists.
//
//   node scripts/cloud-status-counts.mjs            check; exit 1 on a mismatch
//   node scripts/cloud-status-counts.mjs --write    update status.json in place
//   node scripts/cloud-status-counts.mjs --fast     skip the ~2 min SQL batteries
//
// The batteries ARE the authority for their own numbers, so this runs them
// rather than parsing a record of them. `--fast` keeps the ones it skipped.

import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";

const ROOT = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const STATUS = join(ROOT, "cloud.computedriven.com/status.json");
const WRITE = process.argv.includes("--write");
const FAST = process.argv.includes("--fast");

function run(cmd, args, opts = {}) {
  try {
    return { out: execFileSync(cmd, args, {
      cwd: ROOT, encoding: "utf8", stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
      env: { ...process.env, ...(opts.env ?? {}) },
      // The batteries stand up a PostgreSQL cluster each; a short timeout here
      // would report "0 tests" and look like a clean tree.
      timeout: opts.timeout ?? 900_000,
    }), code: 0 };
  } catch (e) {
    return { out: `${e.stdout ?? ""}${e.stderr ?? ""}`, code: e.status ?? 1 };
  }
}

const grabLast = (text, re) => {
  let m, last = null;
  const g = new RegExp(re, "g");
  while ((m = g.exec(text)) !== null) last = m[1];
  return last === null ? null : Number(last);
};

const measured = {};

// Which PostgreSQL the batteries used is THEIR decision, not this script's: both
// shell batteries default to the R33 target (17.x) when it is installed and
// honour CD_PGBIN otherwise. Setting it here as well would be a second place for
// that policy to live, and the two would eventually disagree about which number
// the status page is publishing.
const PGENV = {};

// --- static: things that are just files in the tree -------------------------
measured.migrations = readdirSync(join(ROOT, "worker/migrations"))
  .filter((f) => f.endsWith(".sql")).length;

// Live-falsifier cases. status.json said "Eight questions" against an array of
// NINE for a full round, and the prose gate could not see it because there was
// no derived number to disagree with -- the check compares prose against the
// derived block, so a fact that exists ONLY in prose is invisible to it.
//
//     A DRIFT GATE CAN ONLY CATCH A FACT THAT HAS SOMEWHERE ELSE TO BE RIGHT.
//
// Counted by parsing the id: lines rather than by importing, because the module
// refuses to load without bindings and a counter that needs a Cloudflare
// account is not a counter.
// `[A-Z][0-9]?`, because case D split into D and D2 and a single-letter pattern
// would have reported 9 against an array of 10 -- silently, and in the field
// that exists BECAUSE prose said "Eight" against nine. A deriver with too narrow
// a pattern is a hand-typed number that takes longer to notice.
measured.falsifier_cases = (readFileSync(join(ROOT, "worker/test/live-falsifier.mjs"), "utf8")
  .match(/^\s{4}id:\s*"[A-Z][0-9]?"/gm) ?? []).length;

// FINDING 111, 2026-08-24. THE RUN ORDER IS DERIVED TOO, for the same reason the
// count is. The bundle's prose said `P -> D -> D2 -> ... -> J` while the
// executable had grown to fifteen cases starting at Q — a hand-typed sequence
// that drifted exactly as every hand-typed number in this tree has. The
// falsifier cross-checks SEQUENCE against its own case list and refuses when
// they disagree, so reading it here inherits that check.
measured.falsifier_order = (readFileSync(join(ROOT, "worker/test/live-falsifier.mjs"), "utf8")
  .match(/^export const SEQUENCE = \[([^\]]*)\]/m)?.[1] ?? "")
  .split(",").map((t) => t.trim().replace(/"/g, "")).filter(Boolean).join(" -> ");

// One vector per line inside VECTORS=( ... ). EITHER quote style: one vector is
// single-quoted because its anchor is a JS template literal, and a counter that
// only knew about double quotes would silently report one fewer than exists --
// which is the class of error this whole script was written for.
measured.mutation_vectors = readFileSync(join(ROOT, "worker/test/sabotage.sh"), "utf8")
  .split("\n").filter((l) => /^["'][a-z0-9-]+:::/.test(l)).length;

// --- measured: the suites are the authority for their own totals ------------
const unit = run("npm", ["test", "--prefix", "worker"]);
measured.worker_tests  = grabLast(unit.out, String.raw`(?:ℹ|#) pass (\d+)`);
measured.worker_failed = grabLast(unit.out, String.raw`(?:ℹ|#) fail (\d+)`);

if (!FAST) {
  const mut = run("./worker/test/sabotage.sh", []);
  const v = /(\d+) caught\s+(\d+) missed\s+(\d+) stale\s+\((\d+) vectors\)/.exec(mut.out);
  if (v) {
    measured.mutations_caught = Number(v[1]);
    measured.mutations_missed = Number(v[2]);
    measured.mutations_stale  = Number(v[3]);
    measured.mutations_total  = Number(v[4]);
  }

  // R33 targets 17.x because Hyperdrive documents 9.0-17.x, so the PUBLISHED
  // number must come from the target version when one is installed. Running on
  // 18 and publishing that was defensible while 17 was unavailable; it is not
  // once it is there, because the status page would then report a green run on
  // a major the transport does not claim.
  //
  // `pg_major_tested` used to be a HAND-TYPED field in status.json, in the file
  // whose entire premise is that hand-typed numbers go stale. It is derived from
  // the battery's own banner now.
  const sql = run("./worker/test/tenant-isolation.sh", [], { env: PGENV });
  measured.pg_major_tested = grabLast(stripAnsi(sql.out), String.raw`postgres (\d+)\.\d+ on`);
  const s = /(\d+) passed\s+(\d+) failed(?:\s+(?:\d+) warned)?\s+\((\d+) checks\)/.exec(stripAnsi(sql.out));
  if (s) {
    measured.sql_passed = Number(s[1]);
    measured.sql_failed = Number(s[2]);
    measured.sql_total  = Number(s[3]);
  }

  // Warnings are a third outcome and must not be counted as passes. L7 warns
  // when the battery runs on a PostgreSQL major Hyperdrive does not document --
  // not a schema defect, not a clean bill of health either.
  const w = /(\d+) passed\s+(\d+) failed\s+(\d+) warned/.exec(stripAnsi(sql.out));
  if (w) measured.sql_warned = Number(w[3]);

  const conc = run("./worker/test/concurrency.sh", [], { env: PGENV });
  const c = /(\d+) passed\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(stripAnsi(conc.out));
  if (c) {
    measured.concurrency_passed = Number(c[1]);
    measured.concurrency_failed = Number(c[2]);
  }

  // Each concurrency sabotage mode must break ITS OWN group and leave the others
  // alone. A published "13 passed" says nothing about whether the battery can
  // fail, and a mode that breaks the wrong group is measuring something other
  // than what it claims -- so the CAUGHT/MISSED/MISDIRECTED verdict is counted,
  // not the pass tally.
  measured.concurrency_controls_caught = 0;
  for (const mode of ["lock", "quota", "offer", "observe"]) {
    const r = run("./worker/test/concurrency.sh", [], { env: { ...PGENV, CD_SABOTAGE: mode } });
    if (/control verdict:\s*CAUGHT/.test(stripAnsi(r.out))) measured.concurrency_controls_caught++;
  }
  measured.concurrency_controls_total = 4;

  // The CONTROL runs. These were the numbers that went most stale, because they
  // are the ones nobody re-runs casually -- and a control whose published result
  // is from four migrations ago is not a control.
  const sab = run("./worker/test/tenant-isolation.sh", [], { env: { ...PGENV, CD_SABOTAGE: "1" } });
  const sb = /(\d+) passed\s+(\d+) failed(?:\s+(?:\d+) warned)?\s+\((\d+) checks\)/.exec(stripAnsi(sab.out));
  if (sb) {
    measured.sabotage_passed = Number(sb[1]);
    measured.sabotage_failed = Number(sb[2]);
  }

  // The regression proof: apply the migration set with the FIXES REMOVED and
  // count what breaks. 0014 comes out too, and not because it is a fix under
  // test -- it calls app.membership_role(), which 0010 creates, so a set without
  // 0010 does not APPLY. The first version of this measurement aborted at
  // migration time and would have published a number from a run that never
  // reached a single check.
  const removed = (JSON.parse(readFileSync(STATUS, "utf8")).battery.regression_removed ?? "").match(/\d{4}/g) ?? [];
  if (removed.length) {
    const dir = join(ROOT, "node_modules/.cache/cd-regression");
    run("rm", ["-rf", dir]);
    run("mkdir", ["-p", dir]);
    for (const f of readdirSync(join(ROOT, "worker/migrations"))) {
      if (f.endsWith(".sql") && !removed.some((n) => f.startsWith(n))) {
        run("cp", [join(ROOT, "worker/migrations", f), dir]);
      }
    }
    const reg = run("./worker/test/tenant-isolation.sh", [],
      { env: { ...PGENV, CD_MIGRATIONS: dir, CD_PGPORT: "55451" } });
    const rg = /(\d+) passed\s+(\d+) failed(?:\s+(?:\d+) warned)?\s+\((\d+) checks\)/.exec(stripAnsi(reg.out));
    if (rg) {
      measured.regression_passed = Number(rg[1]);
      measured.regression_failed = Number(rg[2]);
      measured.regression_total  = Number(rg[3]);
    } else {
      // Loud, not silent. A regression run that did not produce a tally usually
      // means the reduced migration set failed to APPLY, and reporting the old
      // number would be reporting a run that never happened.
      process.stdout.write("  \x1b[31mREGRESSION RUN PRODUCED NO TALLY\x1b[0m — " +
        "the reduced migration set probably does not apply. Tail:\n" +
        stripAnsi(reg.out).split("\n").slice(-4).map((l) => `      ${l}`).join("\n") + "\n");
    }
    run("rm", ["-rf", dir]);
  }
}

function stripAnsi(s) {
  // The batteries colour their output when attached to a tty and not otherwise,
  // but a caller may still pipe through something that keeps the codes. Strip
  // rather than depend on which.
  return s.replace(/\[[0-9;]*m/g, "");
}

// --- compare ----------------------------------------------------------------
const status = JSON.parse(readFileSync(STATUS, "utf8"));
const b = status.battery;

// Only the keys this script actually measured. A --fast run must not report the
// numbers it skipped as agreeing, and must not overwrite them with undefined.
const MAP = {
  migrations:            ["migrations",                 measured.migrations],
  worker_tests:          ["worker_tests",               measured.worker_tests],
  worker_failed:         ["worker_failed",              measured.worker_failed],
  mutations_total:       ["worker_mutations_total",     measured.mutations_total],
  mutations_caught:      ["worker_mutations_caught",    measured.mutations_caught],
  mutations_missed:      ["worker_mutations_missed",    measured.mutations_missed],
  sql_total:             ["total",                      measured.sql_total],
  sql_passed:            ["normal_passed",              measured.sql_passed],
  sql_failed:            ["normal_failed",              measured.sql_failed],
  sql_warned:            ["normal_warned",              measured.sql_warned],
  concurrency_passed:    ["concurrency_passed",         measured.concurrency_passed],
  concurrency_failed:    ["concurrency_failed",         measured.concurrency_failed],
  sabotage_passed:       ["sabotage_passed",            measured.sabotage_passed],
  sabotage_failed:       ["sabotage_failed",            measured.sabotage_failed],
  regression_failed:     ["regression_failed",          measured.regression_failed],
  pg_major_tested:       ["pg_major_tested",            measured.pg_major_tested],
  cc_caught:             ["concurrency_controls_caught", measured.concurrency_controls_caught],
  cc_total:              ["concurrency_controls_total",  measured.concurrency_controls_total],
  falsifier_cases:       ["falsifier_cases",             measured.falsifier_cases],
  falsifier_order:       ["falsifier_order",             measured.falsifier_order],
};

let drift = 0;
const rows = [];
for (const [, [key, value]] of Object.entries(MAP)) {
  if (value === undefined || value === null) continue;
  const was = b[key];
  const same = was === value;
  if (!same) drift++;
  rows.push([key, was ?? "(absent)", value, same]);
  if (WRITE) b[key] = value;
}

const W = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => String(r[0]).length));
for (const [key, was, now, same] of rows) {
  process.stdout.write(
    `  ${same ? "\x1b[32mok  \x1b[0m" : "\x1b[31mDRIFT\x1b[0m"} ${String(key).padEnd(W)}  ` +
    // FOUND 2026-08-24, adding case S. The drift separator was ` -> `, which is
    // also the separator INSIDE falsifier_order, so the line read as one
    // thirty-one-case sequence rather than an old value and a new one:
    //
    //     DRIFT falsifier_order  Q -> P -> ... -> N -> S -> Q -> P -> ... -> N
    //
    // A diagnostic whose output is ambiguous about its own structure is a
    // diagnostic that has to be decoded before it can be believed — in the file
    // whose whole job is making published numbers unambiguous. Quoted, so the
    // boundary is visible whatever the value contains.
    `${same ? now : `${JSON.stringify(was)}  ==>  ${JSON.stringify(now)}`}\n`);
}

// A failing suite is not a counting problem, and must not be reported as one.
const broken = (measured.worker_failed ?? 0) + (measured.sql_failed ?? 0) +
               (measured.concurrency_failed ?? 0) + (measured.mutations_missed ?? 0);
if (broken > 0) {
  process.stdout.write(`\n  \x1b[31m${broken} failing check(s)\x1b[0m — the numbers above are ` +
    `accurate about a tree that does not pass.\n`);
}

if (WRITE) {
  b.as_of = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  writeFileSync(STATUS, JSON.stringify(status, null, 2) + "\n");
  process.stdout.write(`\n  wrote ${drift} correction(s) to status.json\n`);
  process.exit(broken > 0 ? 1 : 0);
}

if (drift) {
  process.stdout.write(`\n  \x1b[31m${drift} number(s) in status.json disagree with the tree.\x1b[0m` +
    `  Re-run with --write.\n`);
}
process.exit(drift + broken > 0 ? 1 : 0);
```

### `scripts/check-queue-authority.mjs`

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
// The provider-observation queue is a DEDICATED R2-ONLY AUTHORITY CHANNEL.
// This is the check that says so to the account, not to a document.
//
//   node scripts/check-queue-authority.mjs            check; exit 1 on a violation
//   node scripts/check-queue-authority.mjs --plan     print what it would assert
//
// WHY (finding 84 / R77, 2026-08-23). worker/src/reconcile.mjs correctly trusts
// R2 for `size` and `etag`, derives tenancy from the object key, and refuses a
// body-supplied organization id. What it cannot check is the premise underneath
// all three:
//
//     IT KNOWS A QUEUE DELIVERED SOMETHING SHAPED LIKE AN R2 NOTIFICATION.
//     IT DOES NOT KNOW R2 SENT IT.
//
// Cloudflare's own configuration page says "Any Worker can write to a queue",
// and the R2 event-notification body carries no signature, no nonce and no
// event id -- only account, action, bucket, object{key,size,eTag}, eventTime
// and copySource. So any Worker granted a producer binding on this queue can
// mint occupancy for any tenant whose key format it can guess. Checking the
// `account` field does not help: a producer that can forge the rest of the JSON
// can forge that string too.
//
// The mitigation is not code. It is that NO APPLICATION WORKER EVER RECEIVES
// PRODUCER AUTHORITY TO THIS QUEUE -- and a rule nobody checks is a comment.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// FINDING 88, 2026-08-23, THE ROUND AFTER THIS FILE SHIPPED. IT FALSE-GREENED.
//
// The first version classified producers it recognised and emitted a NOTE for
// anything else, then exited 0. REPRODUCED against a mock Cloudflare response:
//
//     producers: [ {type: r2_bucket, bucket_name: cd-worlds},
//                  {type: future_external_authority} ]
//     ->  NOTE  1 producer(s) of a type this script does not classify
//         OK    ... carries R2 notifications from cd-worlds and nothing else
//         exit 0
//
// and a second reproducer: `{type: r2_bucket}` with NO bucket_name also exited
// 0, because the bucket was only judged wrong when `bucket_name` was truthy AND
// different. Both are exactly the false green the header claims to prevent --
// written by the same hand, in the same file, under that heading.
//
//     A CHECKER THAT CLASSIFIES WHAT IT RECOGNISES AND SHRUGS AT THE REST IS AN
//     ALLOWLIST WRITTEN AS A DENYLIST. THE VOCABULARY MUST BE CLOSED: anything
//     this file does not positively recognise as authorized is a REFUSAL.
//
// So the predicate is now exact, total, and PURE -- exported and unit-tested in
// worker/test/queue-authority.test.mjs, because a gate that can only be
// exercised by having a Cloudflare account is a gate nobody exercises.
//
// IT REFUSES RATHER THAN PASSES WHEN IT CANNOT SEE. No credentials is exit 2
// with a plan; an API error, an unenumerable response, a missing queue and a
// count that disagrees with the list are all exit 1. The only exit 0 is a
// producer list this script enumerated, cross-checked against the provider's
// own total, and found to contain exactly one authorized R2 producer.
//
// IT PROVISIONS NOTHING. Creating the queue and the notification rule is a
// spend decision and belongs to Travis (agents/C-infrastructure.md).

// The two producer types Cloudflare's Queue schema documents. CLOSED on
// purpose: a third type appearing in a future API version must stop this gate,
// not be waved through with a note. Widening it is a deliberate edit with a
// reason, which is the same rule the rest of this stack applies to provider
// vocabulary.
const PRODUCER_TYPES = new Set(["r2_bucket", "worker"]);

/**
 * The whole judgement, as a pure function of the provider's response.
 *
 * @param detail  the Queue object from GET /accounts/{acct}/queues/{queue_id}
 * @param expect  { bucket, consumerScript, queue }  ALL THREE REQUIRED (findings 89-91)
 * @returns { ok, refusals[], observed }   ok === true only when refusals is empty
 */
export function queueAuthorityVerdict(detail, expect) {
  const refusals = [];
  const observed = { producers: [], consumers: [] };

  if (detail === null || typeof detail !== "object") {
    return { ok: false, refusals: ["the queue response was not an object"], observed };
  }

  const producers = detail.producers;
  const total = detail.producers_total_count;

  // Cannot see -> refuse. Cloudflare has reshaped this response before, and
  // reporting an absent list as "no Worker producers" is the false green in its
  // purest form.
  if (!Array.isArray(producers)) {
    refusals.push("the response carried no enumerable producer list, so this check learned nothing" +
                  ` (keys seen: ${Object.keys(detail).join(", ") || "none"})`);
    return { ok: false, refusals, observed };
  }
  observed.producers = producers;

  // The provider's own count against the array we were handed. A paginated or
  // truncated `producers` that disagrees with `producers_total_count` is
  // precisely a case where the missing entries are the dangerous ones.
  if (typeof total !== "number") {
    refusals.push("producers_total_count is absent, so the producer list cannot be cross-checked " +
                  "against the provider's own total");
  } else if (total !== producers.length) {
    refusals.push(`producers_total_count is ${total} but ${producers.length} producer(s) were ` +
                  "returned — the list is incomplete and the missing entries are unexamined");
  }

  const unknown = producers.filter((p) => !PRODUCER_TYPES.has(p?.type));
  if (unknown.length) {
    refusals.push(`${unknown.length} producer(s) of a type this gate does not recognise: ` +
                  unknown.map((p) => JSON.stringify(p?.type ?? null)).join(", ") +
                  " — an unrecognised authority is not an authorized one");
  }

  const workers = producers.filter((p) => p?.type === "worker");
  if (workers.length) {
    refusals.push(`${workers.length} Worker producer(s) hold authority on this queue: ` +
                  workers.map((w) => w.script ?? "(unnamed)").join(", ") +
                  " — each can mint occupancy for any tenant (R77)");
  }

  const buckets = producers.filter((p) => p?.type === "r2_bucket");
  if (buckets.length !== 1) {
    refusals.push(`${buckets.length} R2 bucket producer(s), expected exactly 1`);
  }
  for (const b of buckets) {
    // `!== expect.bucket` rather than `truthy && different`. A producer with no
    // bucket_name at all used to pass, which is the second finding-88
    // reproducer: an unnamed bucket is an unidentified authority.
    if (b.bucket_name !== expect.bucket) {
      refusals.push(`an R2 producer names ${JSON.stringify(b.bucket_name ?? null)}, not ` +
                    `${JSON.stringify(expect.bucket)}`);
    }
  }

  // THE CONSUMER HALF (finding 89, repaired as finding 90).
  //
  // The first version read `c?.script ?? c?.service` -- invented field names,
  // and the unit tests were written against the same invention, so a CORRECTLY
  // provisioned live queue would have been REFUSED by a gate that passed all
  // its own tests. Cloudflare's documented consumer object is:
  //
  //     { consumer_id, created_on, dead_letter_queue, queue_name,
  //       script_name, settings: {...}, type: "worker" }
  //
  // A FIXTURE INVENTED BY THE SAME HAND THAT WROTE THE PREDICATE TESTS THE
  // INVENTION, NOT THE PROVIDER. The last test in
  // worker/test/queue-authority.test.mjs is now that literal documented object,
  // pasted rather than paraphrased.
  //
  // MANDATORY, not optional. It used to be skipped when no expectation was
  // supplied while the overall verdict stayed ok -- so "Case P PASS" could mean
  // "the producer side is clean and nobody looked at the consumer side", which
  // is not what case P says it asserts.
  if (typeof expect.consumerScript !== "string" || expect.consumerScript.trim() === "") {
    refusals.push("no expected consumer Worker was named, so the consumer half of R77 was not " +
                  "checked — case P asserts BOTH sides or it asserts nothing");
    return { ok: false, refusals, observed };
  }

  const consumers = detail.consumers;
  const ctotal = detail.consumers_total_count;
  if (!Array.isArray(consumers)) {
    refusals.push("the response carried no enumerable consumer list");
    return { ok: false, refusals, observed };
  }
  observed.consumers = consumers;

  if (typeof ctotal !== "number") {
    refusals.push("consumers_total_count is absent, so the consumer list cannot be cross-checked");
  } else if (ctotal !== consumers.length) {
    refusals.push(`consumers_total_count is ${ctotal} but ${consumers.length} were returned`);
  }
  if (consumers.length !== 1) {
    refusals.push(`${consumers.length} consumer(s) on the authority channel, expected exactly 1` +
                  (consumers.length === 0 ? " — nothing is receiving this channel" : ""));
  }

  for (const c of consumers) {
    // Closed vocabulary here too. A consumer type this gate does not recognise
    // is an unexamined path from the channel into something.
    if (c?.type !== "worker") {
      refusals.push(`a consumer of type ${JSON.stringify(c?.type ?? null)} — only "worker" is recognised`);
      continue;
    }
    // `script_name` is the documented field. `script` is accepted as an alias
    // because the producer union uses it and one of the two docs pages may be
    // stale -- but an object carrying NEITHER is unidentified, not tolerated.
    const named = c.script_name ?? c.script;
    if (named !== expect.consumerScript) {
      refusals.push(`a consumer names ${JSON.stringify(named ?? null)}, not ` +
                    `${JSON.stringify(expect.consumerScript)}`);
    }
    // FINDING 91. An attestation is meaningful only if its subject is the
    // subject the runtime later trusts. The consumer record states which queue
    // it is attached to; if that is not the channel we came here to check, this
    // gate is proving something true and irrelevant.
    if (expect.queue !== undefined && c.queue_name !== expect.queue) {
      refusals.push(`the consumer is attached to ${JSON.stringify(c.queue_name ?? null)}, not ` +
                    `${JSON.stringify(expect.queue)} — this attestation is about a different channel`);
    }
    // FINDING 92. Cloudflare: "Without a DLQ configured, messages that reach
    // the retry limit are deleted permanently." A deleted provider notification
    // is an occupancy number that silently never arrives -- finding 65 coming
    // back from BELOW the database instead of above it.
    if (typeof c.dead_letter_queue !== "string" || c.dead_letter_queue.trim() === "") {
      refusals.push("the consumer has no dead_letter_queue, so a notification that exhausts " +
                    "max_retries is deleted permanently and the occupancy it carried is lost");
    }
  }

  return { ok: refusals.length === 0, refusals, observed };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// CLI
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// FINDING 105, 2026-08-24. THREE OF THESE USED TO BE HERE:
//
//     PROVIDER_QUEUE      the channel                 <- from the environment
//     CD_R2_BUCKET        the only allowed producer   <- from the environment
//     CD_CONSUMER_SCRIPT  the only allowed consumer   <- from the environment
//
// Finding 91 had already ruled that an attestation's subject must be the
// subject the runtime trusts, and closed it for the queue by renaming the
// variable to PROVIDER_QUEUE — the same NAME the Worker reads, but still the
// caller's VALUE. Two rounds later three more subjects arrived the same way,
// and REPRODUCED: change `[vars] R2_BUCKET` to a foreign bucket and every local
// gate stays green, because nothing compared the two.
//
//     AN ATTESTATION WHOSE SUBJECT IS CALLER-CHOSEN IS A CAPABILITY TO ATTEST
//     THE WRONG SYSTEM.
//
// Subjects now come from scripts/deployment-subjects.mjs and ONLY from there.
// The environment supplies credentials, which are not subjects.
const NEEDED = {
  CF_ACCOUNT_ID:      "Cloudflare account id",
  CF_API_TOKEN:       "API token with Queues:Read (Read is sufficient; do not hand this Edit)",
};
// FINDING 120. `CD_QUEUE_ID` USED TO BE OFFERED HERE AND IT COULD NOT WORK.
// Finding 105 retired every caller-chosen subject, and `deployment-subjects.mjs`
// lists CD_QUEUE_ID among them — so `refuseRetiredSubjectEnv()` below REFUSES
// the run the moment it is set, while this block was still advertising it as a
// supported option and the code below still had a branch for it. Not a hole (the
// refusal happens first) but a dead conceptual branch, which is how a future
// maintainer reintroduces a retired interface believing it is supported. The
// advertisement and the branch are both gone.
const OPTIONAL = {
  CD_CF_API_BASE: "API base override, for the mock the unit tests drive",
};

// FINDING 91. THE CHANNEL IS ONE FACT AND IT HAD THREE SPELLINGS: the Worker's
// env.PROVIDER_QUEUE, wrangler's [[queues.consumers]].queue, and this script's
// own CD_QUEUE_NAME -- three independent strings that happened to agree, with
// nothing making them. Case P could then prove something true about queue A
// while the Worker trusted queue B.
//
//     AN ATTESTATION IS MEANINGFUL ONLY IF ITS SUBJECT IS THE SUBJECT THE
//     RUNTIME LATER TRUSTS.
//
// So CD_QUEUE_NAME is gone and this script reads PROVIDER_QUEUE, the same
// variable name the Worker reads. scripts/check-channel-identity.mjs proves
// wrangler.toml's two spellings agree with it, and runs without an account.

const PLAN = [
  "the producer list was actually enumerated, not assumed empty",
  "producers_total_count agrees with the list that was returned",
  "exactly one producer, type exactly \"r2_bucket\", bucket_name exactly the ACTIVE VERSION's R2_BUCKET binding",
  "zero producers of Worker type; an unrecognised type REFUSES",
  "the consumer list was enumerated and consumers_total_count agrees with it",
  "exactly one consumer, type \"worker\", script_name exactly the ACTIVE VERSION's Worker name",
  "that consumer's queue_name is the ACTIVE VERSION's PROVIDER_QUEUE binding",
  "that consumer has a NON-EMPTY dead_letter_queue (finding 92: without one, an exhausted " +
    "retry deletes the notification permanently)",
  "every subject above came from the ACTIVE WORKER VERSION — not this process's environment (105), and not the manifest (127/135)",
];

import { refuseRetiredSubjectEnv, resolveLiveSubjects } from "./deployment-subjects.mjs";

const isMain = process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`;

if (isMain) {
  const API = process.env.CD_CF_API_BASE ?? "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4";
  const missing = Object.keys(NEEDED).filter((k) => !process.env[k]);

  if (process.argv.includes("--plan") || missing.length) {
    console.log("\n  QUEUE AUTHORITY CHECK — plan only. Nothing has been contacted.\n");
    console.log(`  ${missing.length ? `Not runnable — missing: ${missing.join(", ")}` : "Requested with --plan."}\n`);
    console.log("  It would assert, against the live account:\n");
    for (const p of PLAN) console.log(`     - ${p}`);
    console.log("\n  Needed:\n");
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(NEEDED)) console.log(`     ${k.padEnd(20)} ${v}`);
    console.log("\n  Optional:\n");
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(OPTIONAL)) console.log(`     ${k.padEnd(20)} ${v}`);
    console.log("\n  R77 — delivery identity names the channel that delivered it. The database");
    console.log("  half is worker/migrations/0026; the admission half is the Worker's queue()");
    console.log("  handler; this is the half neither of them can see.\n");
    // 2, not 0 and not 1. Zero would let a CI job that forgot the credentials
    // report this property as HELD; one would be indistinguishable from a real
    // violation. "I could not look" is its own outcome.
    process.exit(missing.length ? 2 : 0);
  }

  const { CF_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_API_TOKEN } = process.env;

  // Subjects from the deployment, never from the caller (finding 105).
  const retired = refuseRetiredSubjectEnv();
  if (retired) { console.error(`\n  REFUSED  ${retired}\n`); process.exit(1); }
  let deployment;
  try {
    // FINDING 127. THE SUBJECT IS RESOLVED HERE, AGAINST THE DEPLOYMENT, NOW.
    // This used to be `requireSubjects()` — the FILE — on the reasoning that
    // case S had already compared the file to the deployment. But a prior check
    // is not a capability: S is separately invocable, `--run` does not exist to
    // sequence them, and the deployment can change in between. The subject has
    // to cross the boundary with the operation that uses it.
    deployment = await resolveLiveSubjects({
      accountId: CF_ACCOUNT_ID, apiToken: CF_API_TOKEN,
    });
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.code === "CD-SUBJ-NOTDEPLOYED") {
      process.stderr.write("\n  NOT RUN  " + e.message + "\n           Exit 2: this gate attests a " +
        "DEPLOYED Worker and there is not one.\n\n");
      process.exit(2);
    }
    process.stderr.write(`\n  REFUSED  ${e.message}\n\n`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
  const { providerQueue: PROVIDER_QUEUE, r2Bucket: CD_R2_BUCKET,
          workerName: CD_CONSUMER_SCRIPT } = deployment.subjects;
  console.log(`  subjects from ${deployment.origin}: queue=${PROVIDER_QUEUE} ` +
              `bucket=${CD_R2_BUCKET} consumer=${CD_CONSUMER_SCRIPT}`);

  async function api(path) {
    const res = await fetch(`${API}/accounts/${CF_ACCOUNT_ID}${path}`, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${CF_API_TOKEN}` },
    });
    const body = await res.json().catch(() => null);
    if (!res.ok || body?.success !== true) {
      const detail = body?.errors?.map((e) => `${e.code} ${e.message}`).join("; ") ?? `HTTP ${res.status}`;
      throw new Error(`Cloudflare API refused ${path}: ${detail}`);
    }
    return body;
  }

  // `GET /queues` is PAGINATED and the first version read one response and
  // searched it. That is fail-safe -- it produces a false "queue absent", not a
  // false green -- but a gate that goes red for a reason unrelated to the
  // property gets ignored. So it pages properly (finding 120 removed the
  // CD_QUEUE_ID shortcut; the subject is not the caller's to choose).
  async function findQueueId() {
    let page = 1;
    for (;;) {
      const body = await api(`/queues?page=${page}&per_page=50`);
      const list = body.result ?? [];
      const hit = list.find((q) => (q.queue_name ?? q.name) === PROVIDER_QUEUE);
      if (hit) return hit.queue_id ?? hit.id;
      const info = body.result_info ?? {};
      const seen = page * (info.per_page ?? list.length ?? 0);
      if (!list.length || (typeof info.total_count === "number" && seen >= info.total_count)) return null;
      if (page > 200) throw new Error("queue listing did not terminate after 200 pages");
      page += 1;
    }
  }

  try {
    const id = await findQueueId();
    if (!id) {
      console.error(`\n  REFUSED  no queue named ${PROVIDER_QUEUE} exists on this account.`);
      console.error("           Not a pass: the channel this control plane trusts is absent.\n");
      process.exit(1);
    }

    const detail = (await api(`/queues/${id}`)).result;

    // FINDING 91. The id we resolved must still name the channel the runtime
    // trusts. Checked here rather than inside the predicate because it is a
    // property of how we FOUND the queue, not of the queue.
    const resolved = detail?.queue_name ?? detail?.name;
    if (resolved !== PROVIDER_QUEUE) {
      console.error(`\n  REFUSED  queue ${id} is named ${JSON.stringify(resolved ?? null)}, not ` +
                    `${JSON.stringify(PROVIDER_QUEUE)}.`);
      console.error("           An attestation about a different channel is worse than none.\n");
      process.exit(1);
    }

    const { ok, refusals, observed } = queueAuthorityVerdict(detail, {
      bucket: CD_R2_BUCKET,
      consumerScript: CD_CONSUMER_SCRIPT,
      queue: PROVIDER_QUEUE,
    });

    console.log(`\n  queue      ${PROVIDER_QUEUE} (${id})`);
    console.log(`  producers  ${observed.producers.length} enumerated` +
                (typeof detail?.producers_total_count === "number"
                   ? ` / ${detail.producers_total_count} reported` : " / total NOT reported"));
    for (const p of observed.producers) {
      console.log(`     ${String(p?.type ?? "?").padEnd(14)} ${p?.bucket_name ?? p?.script ?? ""}`);
    }
    console.log(`  consumers  ${observed.consumers.length} enumerated (expecting only ${CD_CONSUMER_SCRIPT})`);
    for (const c of observed.consumers) {
      console.log(`     ${(c?.script_name ?? c?.script ?? "(unnamed)")}` +
                  `   dlq=${c?.dead_letter_queue || "(NONE)"}   queue=${c?.queue_name ?? "?"}`);
    }

    if (!ok) {
      console.error("\n  REFUSED  the provider-observation queue is not a dedicated R2-only channel:\n");
      for (const r of refusals) console.error(`     - ${r}`);
      console.error("\n  Live falsifier case P. Do not go live on this queue.\n");
      process.exit(1);
    }

    console.log(`\n  OK       ${PROVIDER_QUEUE} carries R2 notifications from ${CD_R2_BUCKET} and`);
    console.log("           nothing else. Re-run on every provisioning change — a producer");
    console.log("           binding added later is exactly as bad as one added now, and");
    console.log("           nothing in the data plane would notice.\n");
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(`\n  REFUSED  ${err.message}`);
    console.error("           An error is not a pass. This property is UNKNOWN until the check runs.\n");
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
```

### `scripts/check-channel-identity.mjs`

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
// THE PROVIDER CHANNEL IS ONE FACT. This refuses when it has more than one
// spelling.
//
//   node scripts/check-channel-identity.mjs      exit 1 on disagreement
//
// FINDING 91, 2026-08-23. The authority channel was named in three independent
// places that happened to agree, with nothing making them:
//
//     worker/wrangler.toml  [vars] PROVIDER_QUEUE      what the runtime trusts
//     worker/wrangler.toml  [[queues.consumers]].queue what actually arrives
//     scripts/check-queue-authority.mjs CD_QUEUE_NAME  what case P attests about
//
// A deployment where case P checks queue A while the Worker trusts queue B is
// one edit away, and case P would pass — proving something true and irrelevant.
//
//     AN ATTESTATION IS MEANINGFUL ONLY IF ITS SUBJECT IS THE SUBJECT THE
//     RUNTIME LATER TRUSTS.
//
// This is R76 one level up. There, a column copying another table's fact had to
// be a foreign key to it or it was a second independent claim; here, a config
// key naming another config key's channel has to be checked against it or it is
// a second independent claim. Same law, different substrate.
//
// The third spelling is gone — case P reads PROVIDER_QUEUE now — so this gate
// closes the remaining two and the DLQ that goes with them. IT NEEDS NO
// ACCOUNT, which is the point: it runs in the same breath as the unit tests
// rather than waiting for provisioning.

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
// ONE READER (finding 98's law, applied to a parser this file used to own). The
// small TOML reader moved to deployment-subjects.mjs when three gates needed it;
// keeping a copy here would have been the same second-independent-claim defect
// this file's own header is about.
import {
  deploymentSubjects, tomlScalars, WRANGLER, ROOT,
} from "./deployment-subjects.mjs";
import { join } from "node:path";

const INDEX = join(ROOT, "worker/src/index.mjs");
const src = readFileSync(WRANGLER, "utf8");
const scalar = (key, opts) => tomlScalars(src, key, opts);

const refusals = [];
const seen = {};

const runtime = scalar("PROVIDER_QUEUE", { section: "[vars]" });
const consumer = scalar("queue", { section: "[[queues.consumers]]" });
const dlq = scalar("dead_letter_queue", { section: "[[queues.consumers]]" });
const bindings = scalar("binding", { section: "[[hyperdrive]]" });

seen["[vars] PROVIDER_QUEUE"] = runtime;
seen["[[queues.consumers]] queue"] = consumer;
seen["[[queues.consumers]] dead_letter_queue"] = dlq;
seen["[[hyperdrive]] binding"] = bindings;

if (runtime.length !== 1) {
  refusals.push(`[vars] PROVIDER_QUEUE appears ${runtime.length} time(s); expected exactly 1 — ` +
                "the runtime's attested channel is the canonical fact and cannot be plural");
}
if (consumer.length !== 1) {
  refusals.push(`[[queues.consumers]] declares ${consumer.length} queue(s); expected exactly 1. ` +
                "A second consumer binding is precisely the drift R77's admission check exists " +
                "for, and it should be a deliberate edit here first");
}
if (runtime.length === 1 && consumer.length === 1 && runtime[0] !== consumer[0]) {
  refusals.push(`the Worker trusts ${JSON.stringify(runtime[0])} but the consumer binding ` +
                `delivers ${JSON.stringify(consumer[0])} — every message would be refused as ` +
                "foreign, and case P would attest about whichever one it was pointed at");
}

// FINDING 92. Cloudflare: "Without a DLQ configured, messages that reach the
// retry limit are deleted permanently." Declared here so the omission is a red
// gate rather than a comment promising to fix it later, which is what it was.
if (dlq.length !== 1 || !dlq[0]?.trim()) {
  refusals.push("the consumer declares no dead_letter_queue; an exhausted retry then DELETES " +
                "the notification, and the occupancy it carried never arrives (finding 92)");
} else if (runtime.length === 1 && dlq[0] === runtime[0]) {
  refusals.push("the dead_letter_queue is the SAME queue as the channel; a failing message " +
                "would be redelivered to the consumer that just failed it, forever");
}

// FINDING 105, 2026-08-24. THE SUBJECT SET, DERIVED ONCE AND CHECKED HERE.
//
// This gate proved the channel was one fact and left every OTHER provider
// subject unexamined. Reproduced: change `[vars] R2_BUCKET` to a foreign bucket
// and this gate stayed green, because nothing in it had ever looked at the
// bucket — so cases P and P2, which took theirs from the environment, could
// attest a bucket the Worker never writes to.
//
// The derivation is now shared, so the coherence check and the live gates read
// the SAME values, and a subject missing here is a subject no live gate can be
// pointed at.
const d = deploymentSubjects(src);
for (const r of d.refusals) refusals.push(r);
seen["[vars] R2_BUCKET"] = d.subjects.r2Bucket ? [d.subjects.r2Bucket] : [];
seen["name (Worker / consumer)"] = d.subjects.workerName ? [d.subjects.workerName] : [];

// The runtime reads env.R2_BUCKET (worker/src/index.mjs). A [vars] entry the
// code never reads, or code reading a var the deployment never sets, are the two
// halves of the same drift.
const js0 = readFileSync(INDEX, "utf8");
if (!js0.includes("env.R2_BUCKET")) {
  refusals.push("worker/src/index.mjs does not read env.R2_BUCKET, but the deployment declares " +
                "it and cases P and P2 attest it — an attested subject the runtime ignores is " +
                "an attestation about nothing (finding 105)");
}

// FINDING 94. Two PostgreSQL authorities need two credentials, and a Hyperdrive
// configuration carries its own origin user. One binding read by both
// connect() and connectJobs() collapses the api/jobs split at the moment the
// driver is written — silently, because both function names still exist.
const NEEDED_BINDINGS = ["HYPERDRIVE_CONTROL", "HYPERDRIVE_JOBS"];
for (const b of NEEDED_BINDINGS) {
  if (!bindings.includes(b)) {
    refusals.push(`no [[hyperdrive]] binding named ${b}; the api and jobs roles need separate ` +
                  "origin credentials or the separation is application convention (finding 94)");
  }
}

// FINDING 95, 2026-08-23, THE ROUND AFTER THIS GATE SHIPPED. IT FALSE-GREENED,
// in the same shape finding 88 caught in check-queue-authority.mjs: it checked
// the NAMES and not what they resolve to. Reproduced by pointing the jobs
// binding at the request binding's id:
//
//     HYPERDRIVE_CONTROL  id = X
//     HYPERDRIVE_JOBS     id = X
//     ->  ok  ... two Hyperdrive authorities        exit 0
//
// Two names over one configuration is ONE credential, which is finding 94
// surviving the fix for finding 94.
//
//     A BINDING NAME IS OURS. THE CREDENTIAL BEHIND IT IS THE PROVIDER'S. A FILE
//     CAN ONLY ATTEST THE FIRST.
//
// So this closes the half that IS in the file — distinct ids — and case Q
// (scripts/check-hyperdrive-authority.mjs) closes the half that is not: that the
// two ids carry two different PostgreSQL users into one database with the SQL
// response cache off. Cache state cannot be checked here at all: Cloudflare
// configures it with `wrangler hyperdrive create --caching-disabled`, on the
// configuration rather than the binding, so no wrangler.toml can ever assert it.
const ids = scalar("id", { section: "[[hyperdrive]]" });
// PRINTED IN FULL, not truncated. A Hyperdrive configuration id is not a secret
// — it lives in a committed wrangler.toml by construction — and the first draft
// elided the last characters, which is precisely where a collision shows.
seen["[[hyperdrive]] id"] = ids;
if (ids.length !== bindings.length) {
  refusals.push(`${bindings.length} [[hyperdrive]] binding(s) declare ${ids.length} id(s); each ` +

  process.stdout.write(`  ${k.padEnd(38)} ${v.length ? v.join(", ") : "(absent)"}\n`);
}

  process.stderr.write("\n  REFUSED  the provider channel and its authorities are not one fact:\n\n");
  for (const r of refusals) process.stderr.write(`     - ${r}\n`);

// authorities", which is a claim about the provider that this file cannot see.
// It can see two bindings naming two distinct configuration ids. Whether those
// ids carry two credentials is case Q's.
process.stdout.write("\n  ok       one channel, one consumer, a distinct DLQ, two distinct " +
                     "Hyperdrive configuration ids,\n           and every provider subject a " +
                     "live gate will attest is named by the deployment\n" +
```

### `scripts/check-hyperdrive-authority.mjs`

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
// THE TWO POSTGRESQL AUTHORITIES ARE TWO CREDENTIALS. This is the check that
// says so to the ACCOUNT, not to wrangler.toml.
//
//   node scripts/check-hyperdrive-authority.mjs           check; exit 1 on a violation
//   node scripts/check-hyperdrive-authority.mjs --plan    print what it would assert
//
// WHY (finding 95, 2026-08-23). R80 split the request role from the observer
// role and check-channel-identity.mjs proved it — at the level of BINDING NAMES.
// Reproduced: point both bindings at the same Hyperdrive id and the gate exits 0
// saying "two Hyperdrive authorities".
//
//     HYPERDRIVE_CONTROL -> config X
//     HYPERDRIVE_JOBS    -> config X          <- passes
//
// That reproduction is now closed in check-channel-identity.mjs, which refuses
// two bindings sharing an id. But the file cannot close the rest, because THE
// PROPERTY IS NOT IN THE FILE:
//
//     two distinct config ids may still authenticate as the SAME PostgreSQL user
//     and caching is configured ON THE HYPERDRIVE CONFIGURATION, not the binding
//
// Cloudflare's caching page is explicit that `--caching-disabled` is a flag on
// `wrangler hyperdrive create/update`, not a key in wrangler.toml. So there is
// no file in this repository that can ever assert cache-disabled. It is provider
// state, and only a provider read can attest it.
//
//     A CONFIG FILE CAN ONLY ATTEST WHAT IT CONTAINS. THE BINDING NAME IS OURS;
//     THE CREDENTIAL AND THE CACHE ARE THE PROVIDER'S.
//
// That is R17's real requirement and the reason it has been un-attested since it
// was ruled. R17: these tenant-sensitive paths must not use Hyperdrive's SQL
// response cache, because Hyperdrive observes `SELECT * FROM cd.worlds` and does
// NOT observe PostgreSQL rewriting it internally to include
// app.current_organization_id() — two tenants issue a byte-identical query
// string and the correct answers differ.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// FINDING 101 — `disabled` IS NOT A REQUIRED FIELD, AND ABSENT MEANS ON.
//
// From Cloudflare's own schema, hyperdrive_hyperdrive-caching-common:
//
//     "disabled": { "description": "Set to true to disable caching of SQL
//                    responses. Default is false.", "type": "boolean" }
//
// with no `required`. So `caching: {}` is a legal response and it means CACHING
// IS ON. A gate written as `caching.disabled !== false` passes on absence and
// attests the opposite of the truth. It is checked as `=== true` below, and
// `caching` absent entirely is a refusal rather than a default.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// FINDING 102 — THE VPC ORIGIN HAS NO HOST, AND FORBIDS TLS ON THE HYPERDRIVE.
//
// CLOUD_V1 §0 puts the control plane on Workers reaching Pigsty over
// Hyperdrive -> Workers VPC -> Cloudflare Tunnel. Cloudflare's schema for that
// origin variant carries `service_id` and NOTHING ELSE — no host, no port — and
// says:
//
//     "TLS settings (mTLS, sslmode) cannot be configured on the Hyperdrive when
//      using a VPC Service origin; TLS must be managed on the VPC Service
//      itself."
//
// Two consequences, both recorded rather than assumed. A check demanding
// `origin.host` would refuse the correct topology; and any plan to pin
// `sslmode=verify-full` on the Hyperdrive config is not available here and has
// to be made on the VPC Service.
//
// **UPDATED 2026-08-24 (finding 106).** That second half was written as a note
// about something nobody asserted. It is now asserted: the VPC Service carries
// `tls_settings.cert_verification_mode`, Cloudflare documents `verify_full` as
// the default and `disabled` as a legal value, and a service with verification
// disabled is a plaintext-trust path to the database this whole file is about.
// Case Q reads the service and refuses `disabled`.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// IT REFUSES RATHER THAN PASSES WHEN IT CANNOT SEE, exactly like
// check-queue-authority.mjs: no credentials is exit 2 with a plan; an API error,
// an unrecognised origin variant, an absent field and a mismatch are all exit 1.
// The predicate is PURE and unit-tested in worker/test/hyperdrive-authority.test.mjs,
// because a gate that can only be exercised by having a Cloudflare account is a
// gate nobody exercises.
//
// IT PROVISIONS NOTHING. Creating a Hyperdrive configuration spends money and
// belongs to Travis (agents/C-infrastructure.md).

// FINDING 105, 2026-08-24. This gate took HYPERDRIVE_CONTROL_ID and
// HYPERDRIVE_JOBS_ID from its invocation environment, so it could inspect two
// pristine configurations while the Worker's bindings pointed elsewhere — a
// perfect attestation about a system nobody deploys. Ids now come from the
// deployment's own [[hyperdrive]] entries.
import { refuseRetiredSubjectEnv, ruledTopology, resolveLiveSubjects } from "./deployment-subjects.mjs";

// The two logins, as 0001 creates them. NOINHERIT role members, so the login
// role is not the privilege role — the login INHERITS the privilege role, and
// which login you are is what decides whether app.observe_storage_object() is
// callable at all.
export const EXPECTED = Object.freeze({
  CONTROL: { binding: "HYPERDRIVE_CONTROL", user: "computedriven_api_login" },
  JOBS: { binding: "HYPERDRIVE_JOBS", user: "computedriven_jobs_login" },
});

// Cloudflare's documented scheme vocabulary, minus mysql. CLOSED: a scheme this
// gate does not recognise is a refusal, not a note (finding 88's law).
const SCHEMES = new Set(["postgres", "postgresql"]);

// FINDING 106, 2026-08-24. THE VARIANT IS NOT A FREE CHOICE — R7 NAMED IT.
//
// The first version of this predicate recognised all three of Cloudflare's
// origin shapes and required only that CONTROL and JOBS reach the SAME one.
// Reproduced by the reviewer and confirmed here: two configurations with
// distinct ids, the two correct logins, the right database, caching disabled —
// and `host: "wrong-public-db.example"`, a PUBLIC INTERNET origin — PASSED.
//
//     A CORRECT PAIR OF CREDENTIALS TO THE WRONG ARCHITECTURE.
//
// CLOUD_V1's ruled path (R7) is Worker -> Hyperdrive -> Workers VPC ->
// Cloudflare Tunnel -> Pigsty. An internet origin means Pigsty is reachable from
// the public internet with a password, which is the thing the Tunnel exists to
// make untrue; an Access origin is a different product with different failure
// modes. Neither is a variant to tolerate — they are configurations that would
// have to be ruled before they could be attested.
//
// So `vpc_service` is REQUIRED, the service_id must be the expected one, and the
// VPC Service itself is a second attestation: the Hyperdrive config only names a
// service_id, and everything R7 actually cares about — which Tunnel, which host,
// which port, what TLS — lives on the service object one level down.
const REQUIRED_VARIANT = "vpc_service";

/**
 * Which origin variant the provider returned, or null.
 *
 * Cloudflare's `origin` is a oneOf over three shapes and they are distinguished
 * by which field is present, not by a discriminator:
 *
 *   internet      host + port
 *   over_access   host + access_client_id       (Cloudflare Tunnel via Access)
 *   vpc_service   service_id, and no host       (CLOUD_V1's topology)
 */
export function originVariant(origin) {
  if (origin === null || typeof origin !== "object") return null;
  if (typeof origin.service_id === "string" && origin.service_id !== "") return "vpc_service";
  if (typeof origin.access_client_id === "string" && origin.access_client_id !== "") return "over_access";
  if (typeof origin.host === "string" && origin.host !== "") return "internet";
  return null;

/** The thing the two configs must agree about: WHICH DATABASE. */
function originTarget(origin, variant) {
  if (variant === "vpc_service") return `vpc:${origin.service_id}`;
  if (variant === "over_access") return `access:${origin.host}`;
  return `net:${origin.host}:${origin.port ?? "?"}`;
}

/**
 * The whole judgement, as a pure function of the provider's two responses.
 *
 * @param control  the Hyperdrive config from GET /accounts/{a}/hyperdrive/configs/{id}
 * @param jobs     the same, for the observer role
 * @param expect   { database }  the origin database both must name. REQUIRED.
 * @returns { ok, refusals[], notes[], observed }   ok === true only when refusals is empty
 */
export function hyperdriveAuthorityVerdict(control, jobs, expect = {}) {
  const refusals = [];
  const notes = [];
  const observed = {};

  for (const [f, why] of [
    ["database", "which origin database to expect"],
    ["vpcServiceId", "which Workers VPC Service the ruled path (R7) goes through"],

    if (typeof expect[f] !== "string" || expect[f].trim() === "") {
      refusals.push(`the check was not told ${why}; an attestation whose subject is unnamed ` +
                    "proves nothing (R77, finding 91)");
    }

  const seen = {};
  for (const [role, cfg] of [["CONTROL", control], ["JOBS", jobs]]) {
    const want = EXPECTED[role];
    if (cfg === null || typeof cfg !== "object") {
      refusals.push(`${want.binding}: the configuration response was not an object, so this ` +
                    "check learned nothing about it");
      continue;
    }
    const s = { id: cfg.id ?? null, user: null, database: null, scheme: null,
                variant: null, target: null, cachingDisabled: null };

    if (typeof cfg.id !== "string" || cfg.id === "") {
      refusals.push(`${want.binding}: the configuration states no id`);
    }

    // ---- the credential ---------------------------------------------------
    const origin = cfg.origin;
    const variant = originVariant(origin);
    s.variant = variant;
    if (variant === null) {
      refusals.push(`${want.binding}: the origin matches none of Cloudflare's three documented ` +
                    "shapes (internet / over-Access / VPC service), so the database it reaches " +
                    `is unidentified (keys seen: ${Object.keys(origin ?? {}).join(", ") || "none"})`);
    } else if (variant !== REQUIRED_VARIANT) {
      // FINDING 106. Not "a different but acceptable topology" — R7 ruled the
      // path, and an internet origin means Pigsty answers the public internet
      // with a password, which is what the Tunnel exists to make untrue.
      refusals.push(`${want.binding}: the origin is a ${variant.replace("_", "-")} origin, not a ` +
                    "Workers VPC service. R7 rules the path Worker -> Hyperdrive -> Workers VPC " +
                    "-> Cloudflare Tunnel -> Pigsty; two correct credentials to the wrong " +
                    "architecture is not the property this gate exists to prove (finding 106)");

      s.target = originTarget(origin, variant);
      seen[role] = s; observed[role] = s;
      continue;
    } else {
      s.target = originTarget(origin, variant);
      s.user = typeof origin.user === "string" ? origin.user : null;
      s.database = typeof origin.database === "string" ? origin.database : null;
      s.scheme = typeof origin.scheme === "string" ? origin.scheme : null;

      if (s.user === null) {
        refusals.push(`${want.binding}: the origin states no user, so which PostgreSQL authority ` +
                      "this configuration carries is unknown");
      } else if (s.user !== want.user) {
        refusals.push(`${want.binding}: origin.user is ${JSON.stringify(s.user)}, expected ` +
                      `${JSON.stringify(want.user)} — the binding name is ours, the credential ` +
                      "is the provider's, and only the second one decides what the connection " +
                      "may execute (finding 95)");
      }
      if (s.database !== expect.database) {
        refusals.push(`${want.binding}: origin.database is ${JSON.stringify(s.database)}, ` +
                      `expected ${JSON.stringify(expect.database)}`);
      }
      if (!SCHEMES.has(s.scheme)) {
        refusals.push(`${want.binding}: origin.scheme is ${JSON.stringify(s.scheme)}, which is ` +
                      "not a PostgreSQL scheme this gate recognises");
      }
      if (origin.service_id !== expect.vpcServiceId) {
        refusals.push(`${want.binding}: origin.service_id is ` +
                      `${JSON.stringify(origin.service_id)}, expected ` +
                      `${JSON.stringify(expect.vpcServiceId)} — a VPC service that is not the ` +
                      "one carrying the Tunnel to Pigsty is a private path to somewhere else");
      }
    }

    // ---- the cache (R17) --------------------------------------------------
    // STRICTLY true. `disabled` is not a required field and Cloudflare documents
    // its default as false, so an absent key means CACHING IS ON (finding 101).
    if (cfg.caching === null || typeof cfg.caching !== "object") {
      refusals.push(`${want.binding}: the configuration states no caching object, so R17 — no ` +
                    "SQL response cache on a tenant-sensitive path — is unattested");
    } else {
      s.cachingDisabled = cfg.caching.disabled ?? null;
      if (cfg.caching.disabled !== true) {
        refusals.push(`${want.binding}: caching.disabled is ` +
                      `${JSON.stringify(cfg.caching.disabled ?? null)}, not true. Cloudflare ` +
                      "documents the default as false, so absent means CACHING IS ON — and " +
                      "Hyperdrive caches by query string, which is byte-identical across tenants " +
                      "for an RLS-filtered SELECT (R17, finding 101)");

      // request path reads would make every occupancy number in the control

  // it. So this gate proves WHICH USER each configuration claims, never that the
  // two secrets differ. The positive/negative witness through each connection —
  // current_user, and the request credential failing to invoke the observer — is
  // the only thing that proves the grant, and it needs the driver.
  notes.push("origin.password is write-only and never returned, so this gate attests the NAMED " +
             "user and not the secret. The privilege witness (current_user; request credential " +
             "cannot EXECUTE app.observe_storage_object(); jobs credential can) is case Q's " +
             "second half and needs the driver.");

 * only that SOME private path exists. Everything R7 actually rules lives on the

 *
 *     { "type": "tcp", "name": "my-postgres-db", "tcp_port": 5432,
 *       "app_protocol": "postgresql",
 *       "host": { "ipv4": "10.0.0.5",
 *                 "network": { "tunnel_id": "0191dce4-..." } },
 *       "tls_settings": { "cert_verification_mode": "verify_ca" } }

 * A hostname target replaces `host.network` with `host.resolver_network`,
 * carrying the same `tunnel_id`. Verification modes are `verify_full` (the
 * documented default), `verify_ca`, and `disabled`.
 *
 * @param service  the VPC Service object
 * @param expect   { serviceId, tunnelId, target, port }  target is an ipv4/ipv6
 *                 address or a hostname; ALL REQUIRED.
 */

 * of address fields the object carries — `dual_stack` is both, and a service
 * carrying both while the ruling says `ipv4` is a service with a second route.
 */

  ipv4:       Object.freeze(["ipv4"]),
  ipv6:       Object.freeze(["ipv6"]),
  dual_stack: Object.freeze(["ipv4", "ipv6"]),
  hostname:   Object.freeze(["hostname"]),

const HOST_ADDRESS_FIELDS = Object.freeze(["ipv4", "ipv6", "hostname"]);
export const TLS_MODES = Object.freeze(["verify_full", "verify_ca", "disabled"]);

/** The variant whose field set is EXACTLY the fields present, or null. */
function hostVariant(present) {
  const key = [...present].sort().join("|");
  for (const [name, fields] of Object.entries(HOST_VARIANTS)) {
    if ([...fields].sort().join("|") === key) return name;
  }
  return null;
}

export function vpcServiceVerdict(service, expect = {}) {
  const refusals = [];
  const notes = [];

                     tunnelId: null, target: null, targets: [], hostVariant: null,
                     certVerification: null };

    const v = expect[f];

    // "every target the service offers is one the ruling names" vacuously false
    // in one direction and unconstrained in the other.
    const unstated = v === undefined || v === null || v === ""
                     || (Array.isArray(v) && v.length === 0);

  //

  // there is no `id` on either variant). The old code read `service.id`, got

  // it was guarded by `service.id !== undefined`. REPRODUCED with a response in
  // the provider's actual vocabulary:

  //     -> ok: true, refusals: [], observed.id: null

  // tests the invention — and the invented spelling then disabled the check that
  // would have caught it. So the field is read by its real name, and its ABSENCE
  // is a refusal: `service_id` is optional in Cloudflare's schema, and an
  // identity we did not read is not an identity that matched.
  observed.id = service.service_id ?? null;

    refusals.push("the VPC Service response carries no service_id, so nothing ties this object to " +
                  `the ${JSON.stringify(expect.serviceId)} the Hyperdrive origin names. Cloudflare ` +
                  "marks the field optional; an unstated identity is not a matching one");

    refusals.push(`the service returned service_id ${JSON.stringify(service.service_id)} but the ` +
                  `Hyperdrive origin names ${JSON.stringify(expect.serviceId)} — this is a reading ` +
                  "of a different service, which is finding 105 one level down");
  }
  if ("id" in service) {
    refusals.push("the response carries an `id` field. Cloudflare's connectivity service object " +
                  "identifies itself with `service_id`; an `id` here means this is not the object " +
                  "this check was written against, and finding 114 was exactly that confusion");
  }

  // Hyperdrive is pointed at something that cannot be a database.
  observed.type = service.type ?? null;
  if (service.type !== "tcp") {
    refusals.push(`the VPC Service type is ${JSON.stringify(service.type ?? null)}, not "tcp" — ` +
                  "PostgreSQL is a TCP service and an http service is not a database");

    refusals.push(`tcp_port is ${JSON.stringify(service.tcp_port ?? null)}, expected ` +
                  `${JSON.stringify(expect.port)}`);

  // private path was built for a database rather than reused from something else.
  observed.appProtocol = service.app_protocol ?? null;
  if (service.app_protocol !== "postgresql") {
    refusals.push(`app_protocol is ${JSON.stringify(service.app_protocol ?? null)}, not ` +
                  '"postgresql"; Cloudflare documents it as optional, and M2.0 requires it so ' +
                  "the service states what it is for");
```
